facts.statement: Anatosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliforms named for its broad, duck-like snout.
facts.quote: Anatosuchus ("duck crocodile", the name from the Latin anas ("duck") and the Greek souchos ("crocodile"), for the broad, duck-like snout)

facts.statement: Anatosuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous

facts.statement: The type species A. minor was named to reflect the animal's small body size.
facts.quote: The type species of Anatosuchus is A. minor, in reference to its small body size.

facts.statement: Fossils of Anatosuchus were found in the Elrhaz and Echkar Formations, dating to the Late Aptian or Early Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was discovered from the upper portion of the Elrhaz Formation and lower portion of Echkar Formation, indicating an Early Cretaceous (Late Aptian or Early Albian) age.

facts.statement: The broad, flattened shape of the Anatosuchus skull developed as the animal matured.
facts.quote: Differences in the skull indicate that the unusual broad, flattened shape developed as the animal grew older.

facts.statement: The premaxillae of Anatosuchus are broad and flat, each holding six recurved teeth that point backward.
facts.quote: The premaxillae are broad and flat, and form a line straight across the front of Anatosuchuss snout; each holds six recurved teeth which point backwards into the mouth.

facts.statement: The maxillae are the largest bones in the Anatosuchus skull, each containing nineteen small recurved teeth.
facts.quote: The maxillae are, by quite a long way, the largest and most expansive bones in the skull; each holds nineteen small recurved teeth.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Anatosuchus bears twenty-one teeth on each side.
facts.quote: The dentary bears twenty-one teeth on each side.

facts.statement: A 11 mm toothless section of the lower jaw likely formed a cutting edge used with the front upper teeth to process prey.
facts.quote: The dentary symphysis has no teeth present to either side of it for 11 mm, but forms a sharpish edge which may have been used with the premaxillary teeth 1-3 for cutting into prey.

facts.statement: Anatosuchus teeth were small, subconical, and showed little wear, suggesting they were not heavily used for grinding.
facts.quote: The teeth have subconical crowns that curve in towards the centre of the mouth; all are fairly small and not very worn, indicating relatively little use.

facts.statement: The largest teeth in the Anatosuchus skull are located at the corners.
facts.quote: The largest teeth are found at the corners of the skull.

facts.statement: Anatosuchus was described by a team of paleontologists led by American Paul Sereno in 2003.
facts.quote: descrito por un equipo de palaeontólogos encabezados por el estadounidense Paul Sereno en 2003

facts.statement: The fossils of Anatosuchus were discovered in Gadoufaoua, Niger.
facts.quote: descubierto en Gadoufaoua, Níger

facts.statement: Anatosuchus was described based on a juvenile specimen.
facts.quote: Fue descrito a partir de un ejemplar joven

facts.statement: The holotype material (MNN GDF603) consists of an almost complete skull with articulated jaws.
facts.quote: El material del holotipo (MNN GDF603), es un cráneo casi completo con las mandíbulas articuladas

facts.statement: Anatosuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the late Aptian or early Albian stages.
facts.quote: pertenece al Cretácico Inferior (Aptiense superior o Albiense inferior)

facts.statement: Anatosuchus lived between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Anatosuchus is an extinct genus of notosuchian crocodile.
facts.quote: es un género extinto de cocodrilo notosuquio

facts.statement: The genus Anatosuchus was named by Sereno et al. in 2003.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Sereno et al., 2003

facts.statement: The only known species is Anatosuchus minor, described by Sereno et al. in 2003.
facts.quote: subdivision: Anatosuchus minor † Sereno et al., 2003

facts.statement: Further research proposed that Anatosuchus is not closely related to Comahuesuchus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el trabajo adicional propuso que Anatosuchus no está estrechamente vinculado a Comahuesuchus

facts.statement: Anatosuchus is classified within the family Uruguaysuchidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Uruguaysuchidae

facts.statement: Anatosuchus had a very broad snout shaped like a duck's bill.
facts.quote: Tenía un hocico muy amplio en forma de pico de pato

facts.statement: The proatlas vertebra is an inverted V-shaped bone with a dorsal keel that is quite large relative to the atlas.
facts.quote: The proatlas is an inverted V-shaped piece of bone with a dorsal keel and is quite large relative to the atlas

facts.statement: The neural spines on the cervical vertebrae grow taller along the series, with the third being twice as tall as long and the seventh almost five times as tall as long.
facts.quote: The axis has a low, subrectangular neural spine; neural spines grow taller along the cervical vertebrae, with that of the third cervical vertebra being twice as tall as long and that of the seventh being almost five times as tall as long

facts.statement: The osteoderms on Anatosuchus are trapezoidal in shape and quite pitted.
facts.quote: The osteoderms are trapezoidal in shape and quite pitted

facts.statement: The manus features very large fourth digits with six phalanges instead of the usual four.
facts.quote: The manus are very large, and have strange fourth digits; each one has six phalanges, rather than the normal four

facts.statement: Despite its duck-like appearance, Anatosuchus is considered to have eaten small aquatic creatures.
facts.quote: Despite its appearance it is considered to have a diet of small, aquatic creatures

facts.statement: The humeri are long, straight, and quite slender, with a width of less than 10% of their length.
facts.quote: The humeri are long and have straight shafts; they are quite slender, with the width less than 10% of the length

facts.statement: The ulnae are relatively curved.
facts.quote: The ulnae are relatively curved

facts.statement: The radiales are strong, heavy bones that are almost as wide as the radii.
facts.quote: The radiales are strong, heavy bones, almost as wide as the radii

facts.statement: It is currently unknown what evolutionary benefit the specialized six-phalanged fourth digits provided.
facts.quote: It is not known what benefit these specialised features conferred

facts.statement: Initial descriptions suggested Anatosuchus formed a monophyletic clade with Comahuesuchus within Notosuchia, though this is disputed.
facts.quote: En la descripción inicial de Anatosuchus, su supuso que formaba un clado con Comahuesuchus, dentro de un menos inclusivo Notosuchia, también encontró que podían ser monofiléticos
